title: Implement a Fenwick Tree
statement:
A Fenwick tree (binary indexed tree) stores an array and supports two operations in logarithmic time: changing one element and computing the sum of a range. Build one and use it to process a sequence of operations.

You are given an array `a` of `n` integers (1-indexed) and then `q` operations of two kinds:

- `1 i v`: add `v` to `a[i]` (a point update; `v` may be negative).
- `2 l r`: report the sum `a[l] + a[l+1] + ... + a[r]` at this moment.

Process the operations in order. For every operation of type 2, print its answer on its own line. Updates are cumulative: later queries see all earlier updates.

**Follow-up:** in the interview the structure itself was asked for; in a real implementation expose `update(i, v)`, `prefix(i)` and `range(l, r)` methods and explain why `i & -i` gives the size of the range each tree cell covers.
input_format: The first line contains `n`. The second line contains `n` integers `a[1..n]`. The third line contains `q`. Each of the next `q` lines is either `1 i v` or `2 l r`.
output_format: For each operation of type 2, in order, print one line with the requested range sum. If there are no type 2 operations, print nothing.

examples.explanation: Initially the total is 3 - 1 + 4 + 1 + 5 = 12. After adding 6 to a[3] the array is 3 -1 10 1 5 and the sum of positions 2..4 is -1 + 10 + 1 = 10. After adding -3 to a[1] the array is 0 -1 10 1 5 and positions 1..3 sum to 0 - 1 + 10 = 9.
The single element is 7. After adding -10 it becomes -3.

hints: A plain array gives O(1) updates but O(n) range sums, and a prefix-sum array gives the opposite trade-off. You need both operations to be fast.
Store in tree[i] the sum of the last `i & -i` elements ending at position i. Updates walk upward with i += i & -i; prefix sums walk downward with i -= i & -i.
A range sum is prefix(r) - prefix(l - 1).
reference:
import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    tree = [0] * (n + 1)
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        tree[i] += int(data[i])
        j = i + (i & -i)
        if j <= n:
            tree[j] += tree[i]
    q = int(data[n + 1])
    p = n + 2
    out = []
    for _ in range(q):
        t = data[p]
        x = int(data[p + 1])
        y = int(data[p + 2])
        p += 3
        if t == b'1':
            while x <= n:
                tree[x] += y
                x += x & -x
        else:
            s = 0
            while y > 0:
                s += tree[y]
                y -= y & -y
            x -= 1
            while x > 0:
                s -= tree[x]
                x -= x & -x
            out.append(s)
    print('\n'.join(map(str, out)))

main()

import sys

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
a = [0] + [int(x) for x in data[1:1 + n]]
q = int(data[n + 1])
p = n + 2
out = []
for _ in range(q):
    t, x, y = int(data[p]), int(data[p + 1]), int(data[p + 2])
    p += 3
    if t == 1:
        a[x] += y
    else:
        out.append(sum(a[x:y + 1]))
print('\n'.join(map(str, out)))
